analysis_steps.goal: Image 340 GHz continuum and fit compact sources

analysis_steps.goal: Make H30alpha cube and moment/PV maps

evidence.quote: The velocity width of the channel maps is $\Delta v=50$ km s$^{-1}$.

validation.value: Positional agreement of continuum and H30a checked using IRS16NE

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate enclosed mass from Keplerian eccentric orbit

method.value: Compare PV shape with calculated Keplerian orbits to get a and e; mass from M ~ a dV^2 (...)^-2 / G

evidence.quote: The observed velocity width is $\Delta V\sim 600$ km s$^{-1}$, and the enclosed mass of the object is estimated to be $M\sim4-7\times10^{4}$ M$_\odot$
for $e=0.96-0.98$ and $a\sim1.4\times10^{17}$ cm

assumptions.value: inclination i~0 deg (edge-on orbit); apoastron PA~60 deg to line of sight

evidence.loc: Compactness of the Ionized Gas toward IRS13E3

why_this_data.value: If an IMBH exists, ALMA can detect ionized gas accreting onto it with large velocity width and compact size

evidence.quote: If the IMBH exists, Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimetr Array (ALMA) can detect the ionized gas accreting onto the IMBH in the IRS13E complex.

referee_caveats_inferred: Orbit parameters chosen by eye with no fit or uncertainties; mass depends strongly on e
Size upper limit from continuum is assumed to equal H30a emitting region
Ionized gas could be a part of the minispiral flow rather than orbiting an IMBH
X-ray association rests on 0.76" absolute astrometric uncertainty and 1999 data
